html.body: Date: 2025-04-17 REMARKSIn response to the non-final Office Action dated March 26, 2025, Applicant amends claims 1-7, 11, 19-27, 29, and 30. Claims 1 and 26 are in independent form. No new matter has been added. Support for the amendments can be found throughout the specification as originally filed, for example at paragraphs [0016], [0069], [0075], [0114], and [0131], and FIG. 6. Claims 1-30 are currently pending.Interview Summary Applicant thanks the Examiner for the courtesy of a telephonic interview held on April 16, 2025. During the interview, the parties discussed proposed amendments, which are reflected above, in light of the 35 U.S.C. 112, 102, and 103 rejections. Agreement was reached that the proposed amendments to dependent claim 4 and "transitional message" in dependent claim 7 overcome the respective 35 U.S.C. 112 rejections. Although agreement was not reached that the proposed amendments overcome the 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 rejections, the examiner recommended adding details about processing the user input and interactions with encyclopedia data entries maintained in the data store. Additional amendments have been made above to reflect the examiner's recommendations.Rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 112 Claims 4 and 7 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112. Without conceding the merits of these rejections and in an effort to advance prosecution, Applicant respectfully submits that these rejections are overcome by the above amendments and the following remarks.Agreement was reached during the interview that the amendments to claim 4 overcome the rejections. Agreement was also reached that defining "transitional message" in amended claim 7 overcomes the respective rejection.Moreover, Applicant respectfully submits that "trimming" in claim 7 is a commonly-used term that a person of ordinary skill in the art (POSITA) would use to refer to shortening or cutting messages or other data for transmission. In the context of Al systems, particularly those involving message-based communication or context-sensitive inference engines, trimming can be understood by a POSITA as a practical technique to manage memory and processing constraints, and therefore to optimize efficiency of communication with downstream components, such as an oracle or other model inference engine. Applicant's Specification as originally filed further defines "trimming" in paragraph [0014]: the "Al game engine can also check if a context can be trimmed in block 518. Referring to both blocks 514 and 518, to ensure that the context provided to the oracle is not overpopulated the Al can be prompted to, after every message, check whether the message history can be trimmed [by] reducing the number of messages that need to be sent to the oracle when generating the next response and/or relevant updates...block 514 aims to clear the majority of the buffer in preparation for a transition" (emphasis added).Applicant's Specification highlights that trimming serves a dual purpose: first, to remove redundant or less relevant information from message history or context to streamline what is being transmitted, and second, to ensure that most pertinent data is provided to the oracle, thereby enhancing performance and relevance of the oracle's response during game world generation and gameplay. A POSITA would readily recognize that such trimming techniques are used in Al systems and communication protocols to reduce computational load and bandwidth usage. Therefore, the term "trimming" in claim 7 would be understood by a POSITA as encompassing these well-known practices of intelligently shortening data prior to transmission.For at least the abovementioned reasons, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of these rejections.Rejections under 35 U.S.C. §§ 102 and 103 Claims 1-10, 23-28, and 30 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102 as allegedly being anticipated by lgnatchenko (US 20240390801, hereinafter "Ignatchenko"). Claims 11-13, 21, 22, and 29 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over lgnatchenko.Without conceding the merits of these rejections and in an effort to advance prosecution, Applicant respectfully submits that these rejections are rendered moot by the above amendments and the following remarks. Applicant requests that these rejections be withdrawn and that the currently pending claims 1-30 are put in condition for allowance.The pending claims are patentable over the asserted reference because the reference does not teach or disclose the features claimed in amended independent claims 1 and 26. For example, amended independent claim 1 recites, among other features:* "generating [a] new JIT game world based on processing, by the oracle, the user input";* "generating, in the data store and based on the user input, datafield entries in an encyclopedia associated with the new JIT game world for the player";* "updating the new JIT game world and the corresponding JIT gameplay based on processing, by the oracle and based on the data field entries in the encyclopedia associated with the new JIT game world for the player that is maintained in the data store, the continuously-received user input and the JIT gameplay";* "updating the new JIT game world and the corresponding JIT gameplay comprises:annotating entities in the new JIT game world with universally unique identifiers (uuids) based on the continuously-received user input, linking the uuids to one or more of the datafield entries in the encyclopedia to establish data connections between the entities in the new JIT game world and the continuously-received user input, and generating, responsive to the continuously-received user input and based on the data connections, actions in the new JIT game world"; and * "generating, based on the JIT gameplay and the actions in the new JIT game world updates to the data field entries in the encyclopedia associated with the new JIT game world for the player that is maintained in the data store" (emphasis added).The asserted reference Ignatchenko describes that it's "universal game server 210 may be used by a game publisher to provide a "base" game and allow for "modders" (or users) to write "mods" (or otherwise make modifications) to the game... Moreover, running third-party code on servers is known to be problematic because of both security and resource consumption issues.In contrast, the solution embodied in the present disclosure addresses these problems.... [The] game server 210 may allow modders to "override" certain parts of server-side assets 220 with their own versions. As used herein, "overriding" may include replacing existing parts, expanding them, and/or otherwise making modifications to one or more server-side assets 220.In some implementations, "overriding" may involve overriding third-party code 244.... [The] third-party code 244 may be run within a sandbox 242 and may be prevented from making potentially-malicious system calls" (emphasis added). Ignatchenko's system assumes the existence of a pre-defined gameframework, which users may then extend or alter. Ignatchenko does not teach or suggest at least Applicant's abovementioned claim features.In contrast, Applicant's claimed technology is directed to a fundamentally different approach in which a game world is built entirely from scratch based on processing ongoing, real- time user input (e.g., "generating [a] new JIT game world based on processing, by the oracle, the user input" recited in amended independent claim 1 (emphasis added)). Rather than starting with a fixed base game, with Applicant's technology, the user inputs are used to generate the content and structure of the game world as the user plays, with each interaction contributing to the creation or refinement of their unique game world (e.g., "updating the new JIT game world and the corresponding JIT gameplay based on processing, by the oracle and based on the data field entries in the encyclopedia associated with the new JIT game world for the player that is maintained in the data store, the continuously-received user input and the JIT gameplay" and "generating, based on the JIT gameplay and the actions in the new JIT game world updates to the datafield entries in the encyclopedia associated with the new JIT game world for the player that is maintained in the data store" in amended independent claim 1 (emphasis added)).Moreover, data entries reflecting the evolving state of the user's game world are continuously generated and stored in a unique encyclopedia tied specifically to that game instance, thereby enabling a dynamic and personalized environment (e.g., "generating, in the data store and based on the user input, data field entries in an encyclopedia associated with the new JIT game world for the player" and where "updating the new JIT game world and the corresponding JIT gameplay comprises: annotating entities in the new JIT game world with universally unique identifiers (uuids) based on the continuously-received user input, linking the uuids to one or more of the datafield entries in the encyclopedia to establish data connections between the entities in the new JIT game world and the continuously-received user input, and generating, responsive to the continuously-received user input and based on the data connections, actions in the new JIT game world" in amended independent claim 1 (emphasis added)). Unlike the Ignatchenko reference, which emphasizes modding pre-existing server-side components under strict constraints, Applicant's claimed technology centers on game world building from the ground up, driven by the user's direct engagement and input.For at least the reasons discussed above, amended independent claims 1 and its dependent claims are patentable over the asserted reference. Since amended independent claim 26 recites similar features as the independent claim 1, amended independent claim 26 and its dependent claims are also patentable over the asserted reference. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of these rejections and allowance of the currently pending claims.Conclusion Applicant respectfully requests prompt consideration and a Notice of Allowance. In the event that no Notice of Allowance will be provided in the next communication, Applicant requests that the Examiner telephone the undersigned attorney (646-746-2405) prior to the next communication so that prosecution on the merits may be expedited.It is believed that all of the pending claims have been addressed. By responding in the foregoing remarks only to particular positions taken in the action, Applicant does not acquiesce with other positions that have not been explicitly addressed. In addition, Applicant's remarks above should not be understood as implying that no other reasons for patentability exist. Finally, Applicant's decision to amend or cancel any claim should not be understood as implying that Applicant agrees with any positions taken in the action with reference to that claim or other claims, or that Applicant adopts or agrees with any position except as specifically stated in this paper. In particular, by amending a claim, Applicant does not necessarily concede that the claim prior to amendment was unpatentable.Apply any necessary charges or credits to Deposit Account 10-0435, referencing the above attorney docket number.Respectfully submitted, Date: 4/17/2025 / Chloe Salome Margulis, Reg.
